note: Every lexical claim in this directory names where it came from. A `source` value is one of these ids. See lexicon/README.md.

curriculum.label: the curriculum
curriculum.detail: A lesson's own theory.md, reference.md or workbook in this repository.
curriculum.authority: canonical — where a dictionary disagrees, the curriculum wins

mw.label: Monier-Williams
mw.detail: A Sanskrit-English Dictionary, Monier-Williams 1899, in the Cologne Digital Sanskrit Dictionaries text (sanskrit-lexicon/csl-orig, v02/mw/mw.txt).

dhatupatha.label: the Dhātu-pāṭha
dhatupatha.detail: The traditional list of verbal roots, in Maṇḍala Pati dāsa's edition (sourceforge.net/p/dhatu-patha), extracted to lexicon/dhatupatha.json. It states each root's gaṇa, pada, iṭ, transitivity and — the reason it earns a place here — its sense in English, which no other source in this repository gives for a root.
dhatupatha.authority: canonical for roots — the whole list, 1,159 entries over 888 roots, is checked in. It agrees with 09-dhatu/reference.md on the gaṇa and the present form of every one of the fifty, and where the two ever disagree the lesson wins and the build says so

mw-parts.label: Monier-Williams, read off the parts
mw-parts.detail: The compound is not split by Monier-Williams in its own headword, but every member of it is a Monier-Williams headword and the reading is the sum of them. Kept apart from `mw` so an analysis that rests on the parts is never reported as one the dictionary states.

notUsed.amarakosa: An Amarakośa pada index (amara_pada: 11,746 rows of Devanagari pada, kāṇḍa.varga.śloka reference, gender, varga, synset head and a Sanskrit semantic category) has since been supplied, and unisonus-00/amarakosha carries a synonyms table but ships no dataset. Still cited nowhere, and for a reason that is about what the text holds rather than whether it is reachable: it gives synset membership in Devanagari and no English sense at all, so it cannot say what a compound member means, which is the one thing the popover needs. Where it would earn its place is verifying the synonym categories of 10-paryaya against the tradition they come from. The categories are cited to the curriculum, which is where this repository actually carries them.
notUsed.apte: Apte 1890 (csl-orig v02/ap90) was consulted while checking senses but is cited nowhere: every claim that survived is one Monier-Williams also carries, and two source ids for one fact is a second thing to keep in step.
notUsed.vidyut: Vidyut's Dhātupāṭha data was not used. The fifty roots this app teaches are the curriculum's own list, with their gaṇa, pada and present form given in 09-dhatu/reference.md, and that list is canonical here.
